title: USBD: Universal Structural Basis Distillation for Source-Free Graph Domain Adaptation

problem.claim: Source-free graph domain adaptation must transfer knowledge across graph datasets without access to source data, but structural shifts can make pseudo-label-based adaptation unreliable.

gap.claim: Existing methods condition adaptation on source-trained GNN smoothness priors, limiting generalization to structurally distinct target graphs.

contributions.claim: USBD learns a universal, structure-agnostic structural basis for source-free graph domain adaptation instead of adapting a biased source model to a specific target.
USBD uses bi-level optimization to distill the source dataset into a compact structural basis whose prototypes span the full Dirichlet energy spectrum.
USBD uses a spectral-aware ensemble that activates prototype combinations according to the target graph's spectral fingerprint.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmarks reportedly show that USBD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially under severe structural shifts.
The authors report superior computational efficiency because adaptation cost is decoupled from target data scale.

narrative_sequence.summary: Source-free graph domain adaptation enables privacy-preserving knowledge transfer across graph datasets.
Source-model smoothness priors limit adaptation to structurally distinct targets and can make pseudo-label adaptation unreliable under topological shifts.
USBD learns a universal structural basis rather than adapting a biased source model to a target.
Bi-level distillation produces prototypes spanning diverse Dirichlet energy frequencies, creating structural coverage for disparate targets.
A spectral-aware ensemble selects prototype combinations from target spectral fingerprints, with reported gains in effectiveness and computational efficiency.

unknowns: Benchmark datasets, baselines, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe the bi-level optimization procedure or prototype count.
Target spectral fingerprint computation and adaptation details are unspecified.
